text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia and Russia on Tuesday signed 16 treaties, covering mostly mutual economic cooperation.
- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said he was very satisfied with negotiations he had held during his three-day visit to Bratislava, ending on Wednesday.
- Economic ministry has worked out a list of goods that should be affected by import deposits. The new measure is expected to come into effect on May 1.

- The next regular session of the Slovak parliament will start on May 13. The session will be interrupted on May 15 for preparations for referenda on NATO membership and direct presidential elections. The session, with 27 items on the preliminary agenda, will resume on May 20.

- The governemnt holds its regular session on Wednesday instead of the usual Tuesday due to the visit of Russian Premier Viktor Chernomyrdin. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic item.
- Slovakia's ambassador to the Czech Republic, Ivan Mjartan, on Tuesday returned to Prague after three weeks of consultations in Bratislava.
- Some $100 million flowed out of the Slovak interbank market on Monday when foreign banks were selling crowns.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Output in the agricultural sector rose some five percent year-on-year in 1996, while output in the food industry increased by 11.1 percent.
- The average monthly wage in Slovakia now totals some 8,100 Slovak crowns, compared with around 10,479 Slovak crowns in the Czech Republic.
- Slovakia will continue to deposit its used nuclear fuel in Russia this year.

- Exports of Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft to the Czech Republic totalled 1.9 billion crowns in the first three months of this year, some 690 million crowns more than in the same period last year.
SME - Some 23 judges have so far signed a letter calling for Minister of Justice Jozef Liscak to resign. The judges say Liscak no longer has their confidence.

- Russian Premier Chernomyrdin rejected a statement by his Slovak counterpart Vladimir Meciar earlier this year that Moscow and Washington had concluded agreement excluding Slovakia from the first wave of NATO eastward enlargement.
- Amnesty International (AI) said there were three people in jail in Slovakia for refusing to attend compulsory military service. The AI demands these people be released from prison.

PRAVDA - The state-run energy monopoly Slovenske Elektrarne has proposed an increase in energy prices of 50 percent for small private customers and 15 percent for cororate clients. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
